sections.h2: What should a Princeton seller handle before closing?
sections.html:
Princeton's own website lists three items that most sellers need: a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate from the Bureau of Fire Safety, a construction records clearance from the Building Department, and a sewer affidavit about sump pumps and roof drains. Each has its own fee and lead time, so start them as soon as a contract is signed.

Princeton is a single municipality in Mercer County. Whether you list with an agent, sell privately or take an as-is cash offer, those three items and the deed recorded in Trenton apply to the house.

sections.h2: How big is Princeton and what do the housing figures look like?
sections.html:
Princeton had 30,681 residents in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 31,469. Housing values run high here, so every percentage point of fees matters to the seller's net.

sections.h2: How did Princeton's borough and township become one municipality?
sections.html:
Princeton Borough and Princeton Township merged and took effect as a single municipality on January 1, 2013. The borough separated from the township in 1894, and the township itself dates to the creation of Mercer County in 1838.

The municipality covers about 18 square miles of land and borders Hopewell, Lawrence and West Windsor in Mercer County, Plainsboro and South Brunswick in Middlesex County, and Franklin and Montgomery in Somerset County. Its ZIP codes run from 08540 to 08544, with 08542 mostly covering the old borough. Cedar Grove, Port Mercer, Princeton Basin and Jugtown are unincorporated communities that keep their own identities within the larger area.

The name Princeton was in use by 1724, and the Battle of Princeton took place in 1777. Nassau Hall briefly served as the national capitol in 1783.

sections.h2: How does the university shape the Princeton housing market?
sections.html:
Princeton University was established in 1746 as the College of New Jersey and moved to Princeton in 1756. Its campus centers on Nassau Street and stretches south. Other institutions in the area include the Institute for Advanced Study, whose Institute Woods hold 800 acres, Princeton Theological Seminary, the Educational Testing Service and the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory.

Census figures for 2022 show about $901.9 million in retail sales and $429.1 million in health care and social assistance receipts for the municipality. The nearest hospital, Penn Medicine Princeton Medical Center, has 355 beds and sits in neighboring Plainsboro.

Ask your agent how the academic calendar affects showing and offer timing on your street.

sections.h2: How do commuters get in and out of Princeton?
sections.html:
US 206 and Route 27 run through town, along with county routes 583, 571 (Washington Road) and 533. Interstates 287 and 295, US 1 and the New Jersey Turnpike are reached through neighboring municipalities. Workers aged 16 and over report a mean commute of 24.2 minutes.

Rail runs on a short shuttle that residents call the Dinky. It covers 2.7 miles of the Princeton Branch to Princeton Junction, where trains join Amtrak's Northeast Corridor and NJ Transit service toward Manhattan. NJ Transit bus 606 runs to Trenton, and Coach USA's route 100 serves midtown New York. Local service comes from the FreeB bus and the university's Tiger Transit.

sections.h2: Which public schools serve Princeton houses?
sections.html:
Princeton Public Schools teach students from pre-kindergarten through grade 12 in six schools. The elementary buildings are Community Park, Johnson Park, Littlebrook and Riverside, followed by Princeton Middle School and Princeton High School. Enrollment was 3,740 in 2020-21, with 1,555 students at the high school, and Cranbury Township sends its high school students to Princeton.

Listing photos and descriptions that name a school should match the district's current attendance zones. Check with the district office before you repeat an assignment in marketing copy.

sections.h2: What are the three Princeton seller requirements and what do they cost?
sections.html:
The municipal Selling Your Home page spells out each item. Fees below come from that page, and they may change, so confirm with each office when you apply.

  • Fire safety: the Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance. Initial inspection costs $50 per unit and includes one reinspection, and each added reinspection costs $50 per unit.
  • Construction records clearance from the Building Department. Request it 11 to 20 business days before closing for $35, 6 to 10 business days out for $70, or 1 to 5 business days out for $125. Pay by check to "Princeton" or with exact cash.
  • Sewer: an Affidavit of Compliance with the Princeton Sewer Operating Committee for sump pumps, roof drains and similar drains, filed for $20. An inspection is available for $50 if the owner asks for one, and the certification takes 7 to 10 business days.

The fire certificate fee depends on timing. It is $45 per unit when the application is completed more than 10 days before closing, $90 per unit between 4 and 10 days before, and $161 per unit with less than 4 days left. Filing early saves $116 per unit. If a building will be torn down or renovated with no change in occupancy, the Bureau of Fire Safety can provide a letter stating that no alarm certificate is required.

sections.h2: What state fees apply to a high-value Princeton sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the realty transfer fee. On sales above $350,000 the Division of Taxation schedule reaches $5.80 per $500 between $850,000 and $1,000,000 and $6.05 per $500 above $1,000,000.

A second charge, the Graduated Percent Fee, applies to residential deeds with consideration above $1,000,000. It is 1% of total consideration up to $2,000,000, 2% above that to $2,500,000, 2.5% to $3,000,000, 3% to $3,500,000 and 3.5% beyond. For illustration only, a $1,050,600 sale would carry about $10,506 in that fee. Form RTF-1EE is attached to every deed over $1,000,000.

Deeds go to the Mercer County Clerk's Office at 209 South Broad Street in Trenton. The clerk notes that deeds recorded after July 10, 2025 with consideration over $1,000,000 fall under the revised state fee.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Princeton homeowner?
sections.html:
A traditional listing gives you exposure to buyers who value the schools and the rail link, but it adds staging, showings and a lender's appraisal. A private sale saves a commission and leaves you to arrange the three city items yourself.

A cash buyer purchasing as-is can shorten the calendar, although the fire certificate, records clearance and sewer affidavit still need to be in hand. If a house will be rebuilt, ask the Building Department what the records clearance covers before you agree to a closing date.

faqs.q: What does Princeton require before I sell my house?
faqs.a: Most sellers need a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the Bureau of Fire Safety, a construction records clearance from the Building Department and a sewer affidavit. Each is filed separately with its own fee, so contact all three offices once you have a closing date.

faqs.q: How much does the Princeton fire safety certificate cost?
faqs.a: The initial inspection is $50 per unit with one reinspection included. The certificate itself costs $45 per unit if you apply more than 10 days before closing, $90 between 4 and 10 days and $161 with less than 4 days left.

faqs.q: How long does the Princeton construction records clearance take?
faqs.a: Request it 11 to 20 business days before closing for $35. The fee rises to $70 at 6 to 10 business days and $125 at 1 to 5 business days, so earlier requests cost less.

faqs.q: Are there extra state fees on a Princeton sale above one million dollars?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller owes the Graduated Percent Fee, which starts at 1% of total consideration for deeds above $1,000,000, in addition to the realty transfer fee. Form RTF-1EE is attached to the deed.

faqs.q: Where is a Princeton deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Mercer County Clerk, 209 South Broad Street, Trenton. Your closing agent normally submits the deed and the state affidavits there.
